title: Single RDP Login Failure
description: A single failed RDP logon (Logon Type 10) attempt. The atomic building block for the brute-force/spray/success-after-failure detections below.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Failed logon events with Logon Type 10.

detection_logic: Filters Security 4625 events where Logon_Type=10.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4625 Logon_Type=10
| table _time, user, src, dest
tuning_guidance: Not independently alertable at scale; feed into RDP-AUTH-002/003 rather than alerting on every occurrence.
investigation_steps: Correlate with subsequent activity from the same source.
response_guidance: No independent response.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Brute Force: High Failure Count from Single Source
description: A single source generated a high volume of RDP logon failures against a single destination in a short window, the core brute-force pattern.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Failed logon event counts per source/destination in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts failed RDP logons per source/destination pair in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4625 Logon_Type=10
| bin _time span=5m
| stats count dc(user) as users values(user) as accounts by _time src dest
| where count >= 10
tuning_guidance: Tune out known vulnerability-scanner/pentest source IPs via an allowlist.
investigation_steps: Identify the source and block at the firewall if unrecognized.
Check whether any attempt succeeded (RDP-AUTH-005).
response_guidance: Block the source IP; if RDP is Internet-exposed, treat with elevated urgency (RDP-NET-001).
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Brute Force: Same Source Against Many Users
description: A single source attempted RDP logon against many distinct user accounts on the same destination, consistent with a username-enumeration or credential-stuffing pattern rather than a single-account brute force.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Distinct-account count per source/destination in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct accounts attempted per source/destination pair in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4625 Logon_Type=10
| bin _time span=5m
| stats dc(user) as distinct_users values(user) as accounts by _time src dest
| where distinct_users >= 8
tuning_guidance: Tune out known credential-stuffing-test/pentest sources.
investigation_steps: Identify the source and block if unrecognized.
Check for any valid usernames leaked among the accounts attempted.
response_guidance: Block the source IP.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Password Spraying
description: A single source attempted RDP logon against many distinct users across multiple destination hosts within a window, the specification's core password-spraying pattern — distinct from RDP-AUTH-003 by spanning multiple targets rather than one.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.description: Distinct-user and distinct-host counts per source in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct users and distinct destination hosts targeted by the same source in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4625 Logon_Type=10
| bin _time span=15m
| stats count dc(user) as distinct_users dc(dest) as target_hosts by _time src
| where distinct_users >= 10 AND target_hosts >= 2
tuning_guidance: Tune out known enterprise vulnerability-management scanning sources.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Identify every account targeted and check for any successes across the fleet.
response_guidance: Block the source; force password resets for any account that may have had a weak/guessable password.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Successful RDP Login Following Repeated Failures
description: A successful RDP logon for a user/source/destination combination that had five or more failures in the preceding window, the highest-priority pure-authentication RDP detection: the credential eventually worked.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Failed-then-successful logon sequence for the same user/source/destination.

detection_logic: Sorts logon events by time and uses streamstats to count preceding failures before a success, flagging where the failure count meets the threshold.
spl:
index=<windows_index> (EventCode=4624 OR EventCode=4625) Logon_Type=10
| eval outcome=if(EventCode=4624,"success","failure")
| sort 0 user src dest _time
| streamstats time_window=15m count(eval(outcome="failure")) as failures by user src dest
| where outcome="success" AND failures>=5
| table _time, user, src, dest, failures
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate for a legitimate user.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed compromised or guessed credential.
Immediately investigate what the session did (RDP-PROC-###).
response_guidance: Disable the account, terminate the session, and force a credential reset before re-enabling.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: First-Seen RDP Source IP for User
description: A user's successful RDP logon originated from a source IP not previously seen for that account, a low-confidence but broad-coverage baseline signal.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Successful logon events joined against a per-user first-seen-source baseline.

detection_logic: Joins successful RDP logon events against a rolling first-seen-source baseline per user.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| lookup user_src_baseline.csv user, src OUTPUT first_seen
| where isnull(first_seen)
| table _time, user, src, dest
tuning_guidance: High false-positive rate for mobile/remote workforces without a maintained baseline; most useful several weeks into monitoring.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the user or manager if unusual.
response_guidance: Low urgency alone; escalate if the user is privileged or the source is geographically implausible.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Rare RDP Source/Destination Pair
description: An RDP connection occurred between a source and destination host that have rarely or never communicated via RDP historically, a general host-pair rarity signal useful for surfacing unusual lateral-movement paths.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Successful logon events joined against a historical host-pair frequency baseline.

detection_logic: Compares the current source/destination pair's historical connection frequency against a low-frequency threshold.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| lookup host_pair_frequency.csv src, dest OUTPUT connection_count
| where connection_count<=2
| table _time, src, dest, connection_count
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained host-pair frequency lookup; high value in smaller/static environments, noisier in large dynamic ones.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the new path.
response_guidance: Low urgency alone; escalate if the destination is Tier-0/Tier-1 infrastructure.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Privileged Account RDP Login
description: An account belonging to a privileged group (Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, server-local Administrators, or an equivalent delegated group) established an RDP session, worth tracking given the elevated impact of any subsequent compromise of that session.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Successful logon events joined against a privileged-group membership lookup.

detection_logic: Joins successful RDP logon events against a privileged-account lookup.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| lookup privileged_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_privileged, privilege_tier
| where is_privileged=1
| table _time, user, src, dest, privilege_tier
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained privileged-account lookup, ideally refreshed from AD group membership on a schedule.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification and correlate with jump-host/PAM usage expectations (RDP-X-###).
response_guidance: Investigate if the source or timing is unusual.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Service Account Interactive RDP Login
description: An account tagged as a non-interactive service/automation account performed an interactive RDP logon (Logon Type 10), which is atypical since service accounts should generally never require an interactive desktop session — a strong indicator of either credential compromise or a policy violation.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Successful RDP logon events joined against a service-account lookup.

detection_logic: Joins successful RDP logon events against a service-account lookup.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| lookup service_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_service_account
| where is_service_account=1
| table _time, user, src, dest
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained service-account lookup; low expected false-positive rate once available.
investigation_steps: Treat as a likely credential-compromise indicator.
Identify who/what used the credential and from where.
response_guidance: Rotate the service account credential and investigate the source host.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Dormant Account RDP Login
description: An account with no RDP logon activity for an extended period (e.g. 30-90 days) suddenly performed an RDP logon, consistent with reactivation of a compromised, forgotten, or intentionally dormant (break-glass) credential.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Successful logon events joined against a per-account last-seen baseline.

detection_logic: Compares each successful logon against the account's last-seen RDP activity and flags large gaps.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| lookup user_last_rdp_activity.csv user OUTPUT last_seen
| eval days_dormant=round((now()-last_seen)/86400,1)
| where days_dormant>30
| table _time, user, src, dest, days_dormant
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained last-seen baseline; expected for legitimate break-glass account testing — confirm against a documented testing schedule.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Verify against HR/offboarding status for the account.
response_guidance: Disable and investigate if unconfirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Recently Reset Password Followed by RDP Login
description: A password reset for an account is followed shortly after by an RDP logon using that account, which is expected for legitimate self-service resets but worth correlating when the reset itself was suspicious (e.g. helpdesk-initiated without the user's knowledge, a common social-engineering pretext).

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Password-reset event (4724/4723) joined with a subsequent RDP logon for the same account.

detection_logic: Sequences a password-reset event with a subsequent RDP logon for the same account within a bounded window.
spl:
index=<windows_index> (EventCode IN (4723,4724)) OR (EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10)
| eval stage=case(EventCode=4723 OR EventCode=4724,"1_reset", true(),"2_rdp_login")
| transaction user maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_reset") endswith=eval(stage="2_rdp_login")
| table _time, user, src, dest, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Correlate with helpdesk ticketing to confirm the reset was legitimately requested by the account owner.
investigation_steps: Verify the password reset was requested by the actual account owner.
response_guidance: If the reset cannot be confirmed as legitimate, treat as a likely social-engineering/account-takeover incident.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Off-Hours RDP Session
description: An RDP session was established outside the user's normal working-hours baseline, a low-confidence supplementary signal that should be tuned per team (global operations/24x7 support desks will legitimately trigger this).

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Successful logon events joined against a per-user working-hours baseline.

detection_logic: Compares logon timestamps against each user's learned working-hours baseline.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| lookup user_working_hours.csv user OUTPUT normal_start, normal_end
| eval hour=strftime(_time,"%H")
| where hour<normal_start OR hour>normal_end
| table _time, user, src, dest
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained working-hours baseline; expect high false positives for global/24x7 teams unless tuned per role.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Low urgency alone; escalate if the account is privileged or the destination is Tier-0.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Fan-Out: One Source to Many Destinations
description: A single user/source host RDP'd into an unusually large number of distinct destination hosts within a short window, one of the highest-value lateral-movement signals in this catalogue — legitimate administration is normally scoped to a handful of systems at a time.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.description: Distinct-destination count per user/source in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct destination hosts RDP'd into by the same user/source in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| bin _time span=30m
| stats dc(dest) as rdp_targets values(dest) as targets by _time user src
| where rdp_targets >= 5
tuning_guidance: Tune out known fleet-management/patching automation accounts and jump-host service accounts.
investigation_steps: Identify every target host and confirm business justification.
Treat as a live incident if the account/source is unexpected.
response_guidance: Disable the account and isolate the source host if unconfirmed.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Fan-In: Many Sources to One Destination
description: An unusually large number of distinct source hosts RDP'd into the same destination in a short window. Can be legitimate for a shared admin jump server or RDS farm, or can indicate a compromised terminal server being used as a staging point, or an attacker enumerating access from many compromised hosts.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Distinct-source count per destination in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct source hosts RDPing into the same destination in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| bin _time span=30m
| stats dc(src) as source_count values(src) as sources by _time dest
| where source_count >= 10
tuning_guidance: Tune per destination role; known jump hosts/RDS farms should be baselined separately with a higher threshold.
investigation_steps: Confirm the destination's expected role (jump host vs. general endpoint).
response_guidance: Investigate if the destination is not an expected shared-access host.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Same Privileged Account RDP Across Many Hosts
description: A privileged account RDP'd across an unusually large number of distinct hosts in a short window, combining the severity of RDP-001 with the elevated impact of a privileged credential.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.path: Security, aggregated across hosts, joined against a privileged-account lookup
data_sources.description: Distinct-destination count for privileged accounts specifically.

detection_logic: Counts distinct destination hosts for privileged accounts specifically, using a lower threshold than the general RDP-001.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| lookup privileged_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_privileged
| where is_privileged=1
| bin _time span=30m
| stats dc(dest) as rdp_targets by _time user
| where rdp_targets >= 3
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained privileged-account lookup; tune out approved PAM/bastion-driven fan-out.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident given the privilege level.
Confirm this matches an approved administrative task, ideally with PAM checkout records.
response_guidance: Disable the account and investigate if unconfirmed.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Concurrent RDP Sessions for Same User from Multiple Source IPs
description: The same account has active RDP sessions from more than one source IP simultaneously, which is atypical for a single human operator and can indicate credential sharing or compromise.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Overlapping active-session windows per user from distinct source IPs.

detection_logic: Identifies time-overlapping RDP sessions for the same user from distinct source IPs.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| stats dc(src) as distinct_sources, values(src) as sources by user, dest, _time
| where distinct_sources>1
tuning_guidance: Correlate with known multi-monitor/multi-device users and citrix-style shared-desktop configurations before escalating.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the user whether both sessions are legitimate.
response_guidance: Terminate the unconfirmed session and investigate.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Impossible/Unlikely RDP Movement (GeoIP)
description: Two RDP source IPs for the same account, in close time proximity, resolve to geographies that could not plausibly be reached by the same person in the elapsed time — the classic impossible-travel pattern applied to RDP source IPs.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log + GeoIP enrichment
data_sources.path: Successive RDP logons for the same user enriched with source-IP geolocation
data_sources.description: Requires GeoIP enrichment.

detection_logic: Computes elapsed time and geographic distance between successive RDP logons for the same user and flags implausible travel speed.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| iplocation src
| sort 0 user _time
| streamstats current=f last(src) as prev_src, last(Country) as prev_country, last(_time) as prev_time by user
| where isnotnull(prev_country) AND Country!=prev_country
| eval hours_elapsed=round((_time-prev_time)/3600,1)
| where hours_elapsed<2
| table _time, user, src, Country, prev_src, prev_country, hours_elapsed
tuning_guidance: Requires GeoIP enrichment; exclude known VPN egress points that can cause false geo-jumps.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the user which location/session is legitimate.
response_guidance: Disable the account and force a credential reset if unconfirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: VPN Login Followed by RDP Fan-Out
description: A VPN login is followed by the same user RDPing into an unusually large number of internal hosts, correlating remote-access establishment with the resulting lateral-movement fan-out for a more complete incident view than RDP-001 alone.

data_sources.name: VPN log + Security Event Log
data_sources.path: VPN success event joined with subsequent RDP fan-out for the same user
data_sources.description: Cross-source correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences a VPN login success event with a subsequent RDP fan-out pattern (per RDP-001's threshold) for the same user within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<vpn_index> action="success") OR (index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10)
| eval stage=case(index=<vpn_index>,"1_vpn", true(),"2_rdp")
| transaction user maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_vpn")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| stats dc(dest) as targets by user
| where targets>=3
tuning_guidance: Tune out known remote-admin workflows using an approved VPN-to-jump-host path.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident if the VPN source or user is unexpected.
response_guidance: Disable the VPN and domain accounts and investigate.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

title: RDP to Domain Controller
description: An RDP session was established to a domain controller, one of the specification's named Tier-0 destinations — DC compromise via RDP is one of the most severe possible outcomes given the resulting Active Directory control.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Successful RDP logon events joined against a domain-controller asset-role lookup.

detection_logic: Joins successful RDP logon events against a domain-controller asset-role lookup.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| lookup asset_roles.csv host as dest OUTPUT role
| where role="domain_controller"
| table _time, user, src, dest, role
tuning_guidance: Expected for the small set of DC administrators via an approved jump host; require a change ticket outside maintenance windows.
investigation_steps: Confirm the source is an approved DC-administration jump host.
Verify against a change ticket if outside a maintenance window.
response_guidance: Treat unconfirmed access as a critical incident; disable the account and isolate the DC's network access pending investigation.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP to Domain Controller from Non-Jump-Host Source
description: An RDP session to a domain controller originated from a source host not on the approved DC-administration jump-host allowlist, sharpening RDP-007 to distinguish approved-path access from a direct/bypass connection.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: RDP-to-DC events joined against an approved-jump-host allowlist.

detection_logic: Joins RDP-to-DC events against an approved-jump-host allowlist and flags misses.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| lookup asset_roles.csv host as dest OUTPUT role
| where role="domain_controller"
| lookup approved_dc_jump_hosts.csv src OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, user, src, dest
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained jump-host allowlist; treat as a critical bypass indicator once available.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Identify why the approved jump host was bypassed.
response_guidance: Full incident response.

data_sources.description: RDP logon events joined against an identity-infrastructure asset-role lookup.

detection_logic: Joins successful RDP logon events against an identity-infrastructure asset-role lookup.

| lookup asset_roles.csv host as dest OUTPUT role
| where role IN ("adcs","adfs","entra_connect","pam_server")

tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained identity-infrastructure asset lookup; expected for a small set of identity administrators via an approved path.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification and approved-path usage.
response_guidance: Investigate unconfirmed access as a critical incident.

title: RDP to Security Infrastructure (SIEM, EDR Management, Backup)
description: An RDP session was established to a host tagged as security tooling (SIEM, EDR management console, vulnerability scanner, or backup server) — compromise of these platforms can blind detection capability or destroy recovery options.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: RDP logon events joined against a security-infrastructure asset-role lookup.

detection_logic: Joins successful RDP logon events against a security-infrastructure asset-role lookup.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| lookup asset_roles.csv host as dest OUTPUT role
| where role IN ("siem","edr_management","vuln_scanner","backup_server")
| table _time, user, src, dest, role
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained security-infrastructure asset lookup.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification and approved-path usage.
response_guidance: Investigate unconfirmed access as a critical incident.
