title: RDP Initiated from Server to Workstation
description: An RDP session was initiated from a server-role host to a workstation, the reverse of the typical administrative direction and worth scrutiny — servers reaching out to user workstations is atypical unless part of an approved support workflow.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: RDP logon events joined against asset-role lookups for both source and destination.

detection_logic: Joins RDP logon events against asset-role lookups and flags a server-to-workstation direction.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| lookup asset_roles.csv host as src OUTPUT role as src_role
| lookup asset_roles.csv host as dest OUTPUT role as dest_role
| where src_role="server" AND dest_role="workstation"
| table _time, user, src, dest
tuning_guidance: Expected for a legitimate helpdesk/support-tooling server; tune out known support consoles.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed, especially if the server is not a known support tool.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Privileged User RDP Directly to Server Bypassing PAM Bastion
description: A privileged user's RDP session to a server has no corresponding PAM checkout/session record, indicating direct access that bypasses the organization's Privileged Access Management bastion — undermining the audit trail and just-in-time access controls PAM is meant to provide.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log + PAM audit log
data_sources.path: RDP logon events for privileged accounts cross-referenced against PAM session records
data_sources.description: Requires PAM integration.

detection_logic: Joins privileged-account RDP logon events against PAM session records and flags logons with no matching PAM checkout.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| lookup privileged_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_privileged
| where is_privileged=1
| lookup pam_sessions.csv user, dest, _time OUTPUT pam_session_id
| where isnull(pam_session_id)
| table _time, user, src, dest
tuning_guidance: Requires PAM integration with a queryable session-record export; very high value once available.
investigation_steps: Confirm the access was not routed through PAM and determine why.
response_guidance: Enforce PAM-only access for the account going forward; investigate the specific bypass.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Inbound RDP from Internet
description: An inbound TCP/3389 connection was permitted from a public/untrusted (Internet) source address, exposing RDP directly to the widest possible attacker population. Treated as Critical unless explicitly approved, per the specification's own instruction.

data_sources.name: Firewall traffic log
data_sources.path: Firewall session log for inbound TCP/3389
data_sources.description: Inbound connection events from untrusted zones.

detection_logic: Filters firewall traffic logs for inbound TCP/3389 sessions from a zone tagged untrusted/Internet.
spl:
index=<firewall_index> action="allowed" dest_port=3389 protocol="tcp" src_zone="untrust"
| table _time, src_ip, dest_ip, dest_port
tuning_guidance: Maintain an explicit approved-exception list (e.g. an RD Gateway's public-facing IP, which should be the only legitimate Internet-facing RDP-adjacent exposure); alert on everything else.
investigation_steps: Treat as a critical exposure finding regardless of whether an attack is currently observed.
Verify NLA and strong authentication are enforced if this exposure is intentional.
response_guidance: Close the exposure immediately unless it is the organization's approved, monitored RD Gateway.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1133: External Remote Services

author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Firewall Rule Exposing RDP
description: A firewall rule change newly permits RDP traffic from a broader source than previously configured, actively creating new exposure — worth alerting on the configuration change itself rather than waiting to observe the resulting traffic (RDP-NET-001).

data_sources.name: Firewall change log
data_sources.description: Rule-change events.

detection_logic: Filters firewall rule-change events referencing TCP/3389 that widen the permitted source.
spl:
index=<firewall_index> action="rule_changed" dest_port=3389
| table _time, user, old_source, new_source
tuning_guidance: Confirm against network-change tickets; treat any widening to include untrusted/Internet zones as critical.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the rule change.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Port Scan (3389) Across Multiple Hosts
description: A single source probed TCP/3389 against many distinct destination hosts in a short window, consistent with an attacker (internal or external) enumerating RDP-listening hosts ahead of a targeted attack.

data_sources.name: Firewall/network telemetry
data_sources.path: Connection attempts to TCP/3389 across many destinations from one source
data_sources.description: Distinct-destination count per source in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct destination IPs receiving a TCP/3389 connection attempt from the same source in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<network_index> dest_port=3389 protocol="tcp"
| bin _time span=5m
| stats dc(dest_ip) as targets by _time src_ip
| where targets>=20
tuning_guidance: Tune out known internal vulnerability-scanning sources.
investigation_steps: Identify the source and block if unrecognized.
Check for subsequent authentication attempts against the scanned hosts.
response_guidance: Block the source; investigate any hosts subsequently targeted with authentication attempts.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1046: Network Service Discovery

author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Scan Followed by Authentication Attempts
description: An RDP port-scan burst from a source (RDP-NET-003) is followed by that same source generating RDP authentication attempts against one or more of the scanned hosts, confirming the scan was reconnaissance for a subsequent attack rather than incidental network noise.

data_sources.name: Firewall/network telemetry + Security Event Log
data_sources.path: Port-scan burst joined with subsequent RDP authentication attempts from the same source
data_sources.description: Cross-source correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences an RDP port-scan burst with subsequent RDP authentication-failure events from the same source within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<network_index> dest_port=3389 protocol="tcp") OR (index=<windows_index> EventCode=4625 Logon_Type=10)
| eval stage=case(dest_port=3389,"1_scan", true(),"2_auth_attempt")
| transaction src_ip maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_scan") endswith=eval(stage="2_auth_attempt")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, src_ip, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; treat as a confirmed targeted attack attempt.
investigation_steps: Block the source immediately.
Check for any successful authentication among the targeted hosts.
response_guidance: Block the source; investigate every targeted host for a successful login.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1046: Network Service Discovery

author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Tunneled via SSH
description: Network or process telemetry indicates RDP traffic is being transported through an SSH local/remote port-forward tunnel, which can bypass firewall rules scoped only to raw TCP/3389 and complicate network-based detection.

data_sources.name: Zeek/NDR + EDR process telemetry
data_sources.path: SSH sessions carrying RDP-protocol traffic on a forwarded local port
data_sources.description: Requires protocol-aware network telemetry or EDR visibility into SSH client forwarding flags.

detection_logic: Filters process-creation events for SSH clients invoked with local/remote port-forwarding flags targeting port 3389, or NDR application-identification showing RDP protocol on a non-standard/tunneled session.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=1 process_name IN ("ssh.exe","plink.exe")
| where match(command_line, "-L\s+\d+:\S+:3389") OR match(command_line, "-R\s+\d+:\S+:3389")
| table _time, host, process_name, command_line
tuning_guidance: Tune out known legitimate administrative SSH-tunneling workflows.
investigation_steps: Identify the tunnel endpoint and the ultimate RDP destination.
response_guidance: Terminate the tunnel and investigate if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: netsh interface portproxy Forwarding to Port 3389
description: The specification's named high-priority tunneling sequence: netsh interface portproxy was used to configure port forwarding to 3389, a native-Windows-tool technique to relay RDP traffic through an intermediate host without installing any third-party tunneling software, evading tooling-based detection.

data_sources.name: Security 4688 / Sysmon Event ID 1 + Registry
data_sources.path: netsh.exe process creation with portproxy arguments targeting port 3389
data_sources.description: Process command-line telemetry.

detection_logic: Filters process-creation events for netsh.exe invocations configuring portproxy rules that reference port 3389.
spl:
index=<windows_index> (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4688 OR sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=1) process_name="netsh.exe" command_line="*portproxy*"
| where match(command_line, "connectport=3389") OR match(command_line, "listenport=3389")
| table _time, host, user, command_line
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume from legitimate administration; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Identify the forwarding chain's ultimate source and destination.
response_guidance: Remove the portproxy rule and investigate the host as potentially compromised.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Known Tunneling Tool Execution (chisel/ligolo/plink)
description: A known third-party tunneling utility (chisel, ligolo, plink, or similar) was executed, a common technique to establish a covert path for RDP or other protocols across network boundaries that firewall rules aren't scoped to catch.

data_sources.name: Security 4688 / Sysmon Event ID 1
data_sources.path: Process creation events for known tunneling tool binaries
data_sources.description: Process-name and hash-based detection.

detection_logic: Filters process-creation events for a watch-list of known tunneling tool executable names.
spl:
index=<windows_index> (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4688 OR sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=1)
process_name IN ("chisel.exe","ligolo.exe","ligolo-ng.exe","plink.exe")
| table _time, host, user, process_name
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; these tools have essentially no routine enterprise use case.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed live incident.
Identify the tunnel's purpose and destination.
response_guidance: Isolate the host immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: SOCKS Proxy Established Ahead of RDP Session
description: A SOCKS proxy connection is established shortly before an RDP session traverses through the same host, consistent with an attacker using proxy tooling to reach an RDP target that is not directly network-reachable from their actual position.

data_sources.name: Zeek/NDR SOCKS detection
data_sources.path: SOCKS handshake telemetry joined with a subsequent RDP session through the same relay host
data_sources.description: Requires protocol-aware network telemetry.

detection_logic: Sequences a SOCKS proxy handshake with a subsequent RDP session through the same relay host within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<network_index> sourcetype="zeek:socks") OR (index=<network_index> dest_port=3389)
| eval stage=case(sourcetype="zeek:socks","1_socks", true(),"2_rdp")
| transaction relay_host maxspan=15m startswith=eval(stage="1_socks") endswith=eval(stage="2_rdp")
| table _time, relay_host, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Requires protocol-aware network telemetry (Zeek); tune out approved corporate proxy infrastructure.
investigation_steps: Identify the ultimate source and destination of the proxied RDP session.
response_guidance: Investigate as a potential covert access path.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP-Like Traffic Observed on Non-Standard Port
description: Network Detection and Response (NDR) application-layer protocol identification recognizes RDP-protocol traffic (the RDP connection handshake) on a TCP port other than 3389, consistent with an attacker deliberately using a non-standard listening port to evade port-based firewall and detection rules.

data_sources.name: Zeek/Suricata protocol identification
data_sources.path: Application-layer-identified RDP sessions filtered to non-3389 destination ports
data_sources.description: Requires protocol-aware (not port-based) detection.

detection_logic: Filters NDR protocol-identification events for RDP sessions where the destination port is not 3389.
spl:
index=<network_index> sourcetype IN ("zeek:rdp","suricata") app_proto="rdp"
| where dest_port!=3389
| table _time, src_ip, dest_ip, dest_port
tuning_guidance: Does not claim reliable detection via port-based filtering alone — this specifically requires application-layer protocol identification (NDR); this library does not claim Windows RDP logs alone can produce this detection.
investigation_steps: Identify the destination host and correlate with RDP-CFG-### port-change detections
response_guidance: Investigate if the port change was not an approved administrative action.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP TLS Certificate Fingerprint Changed Unexpectedly
description: The TLS/RDP certificate fingerprint presented by a server changed without a corresponding certificate-management change ticket, which can indicate a man-in-the-middle proxy intercepting RDP sessions or an unmanaged/self-signed certificate replacement.

data_sources.name: Zeek RDP certificate telemetry
data_sources.path: RDP/TLS certificate fingerprint observed per destination host
data_sources.description: Requires protocol-aware certificate extraction.

detection_logic: Compares the observed certificate fingerprint per destination against a rolling baseline and flags unexpected changes.
spl:
index=<network_index> sourcetype="zeek:rdp"
| lookup rdp_cert_baseline.csv dest_ip OUTPUT expected_fingerprint
| where cert_fingerprint!=expected_fingerprint
| table _time, dest_ip, cert_fingerprint, expected_fingerprint
tuning_guidance: Requires protocol-aware certificate telemetry and a maintained baseline; correlate with legitimate certificate-rotation change tickets.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the certificate change.
If unconfirmed, treat as a possible MITM interception.
response_guidance: Investigate the network path between clients and the affected server if unconfirmed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RD Gateway Traffic to Unapproved Internal Target
description: An RD Gateway session's internal target host is outside the resource authorization policy's intended scope (per an independent asset-role check), which can indicate a Resource Authorization Policy misconfiguration or an attacker exploiting an overly broad policy.

data_sources.name: RD Gateway Operational Log
data_sources.description: Gateway session events joined against an approved-target lookup.

detection_logic: Joins RD Gateway session events against an approved-internal-target lookup.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-Gateway/Operational" EventCode=302
| lookup rdgw_approved_targets.csv internal_target OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, user, src, internal_target
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained approved-target lookup independent of the RAP configuration itself, to catch RAP misconfigurations.
investigation_steps: Review the Resource Authorization Policy for over-broad scoping
response_guidance: Tighten the RAP if the access was unintended.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: RD Gateway Single User Accessing Many Internal Servers
description: A single RD Gateway user accessed an unusually large number of distinct internal targets in a short window, the RD-Gateway-specific analogue of RDP-001's fan-out detection.

data_sources.name: RD Gateway Operational Log
data_sources.description: Distinct-internal-target count per user in a rolling window.

detection_logic: Counts distinct internal targets accessed via RD Gateway by the same user in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-Gateway/Operational" EventCode=302
| bin _time span=30m
| stats dc(internal_target) as targets by _time user
| where targets>=5
tuning_guidance: Tune out known bulk-administration accounts.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for accessing this many internal systems.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: RD Gateway Authentication Failure Threshold
description: Repeated authentication failures against RD Gateway from a single source, the Gateway-specific analogue of RDP-AUTH-002 — since RD Gateway is frequently the one RDP-adjacent service intentionally exposed to the Internet, this is a high-priority external-facing brute-force detection.

data_sources.name: RD Gateway Operational Log
data_sources.description: Authentication failure events.

detection_logic: Counts RD Gateway authentication failures per source in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-Gateway/Operational" EventCode=200
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count dc(user) as users by _time src
| where count>=10
tuning_guidance: Given RD Gateway's frequent Internet exposure, expect background scanning noise; tune against a reasonable baseline while keeping this Essential.
investigation_steps: Block the source IP at the Gateway's network boundary.
response_guidance: Block the source; verify NLA and account lockout policy are enforced.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Successful RD Gateway Auth After Repeated Failures
description: A successful RD Gateway authentication for a user/source that had repeated prior failures — the Gateway-specific analogue of RDP-AUTH-005, and higher priority given RD Gateway is typically the Internet-facing entry point.

data_sources.name: RD Gateway Operational Log
data_sources.description: Failed-then-successful authentication sequence.

detection_logic: Sorts Gateway authentication events by time and uses streamstats to count preceding failures before a success.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-Gateway/Operational" EventCode IN (200,201)
| eval outcome=if(EventCode=201,"success","failure")
| sort 0 user src _time
| streamstats time_window=10m count(eval(outcome="failure")) as failures by user src
| where outcome="success" AND failures>=5
| table _time, user, src, failures
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed compromised or guessed credential.
Immediately investigate the resulting internal RDP session (RDP-NET-012).
response_guidance: Disable the account and terminate the Gateway session before it can reach any internal target.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New External Source for RD Gateway Access
description: A successful RD Gateway authentication originated from a source IP/geography not previously seen for the connecting user.

data_sources.name: RD Gateway Operational Log
data_sources.description: Authentication success events joined against a first-seen-source baseline.

detection_logic: Joins Gateway authentication success events against a rolling first-seen-source baseline per user.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-Gateway/Operational" EventCode=201
| lookup user_gw_src_baseline.csv user, src OUTPUT first_seen
| where isnull(first_seen)
| table _time, user, src
tuning_guidance: High false-positive rate for remote/mobile workforces; most useful several weeks into monitoring.
investigation_steps: Confirm with the user if unusual.
response_guidance: Low urgency alone; escalate for privileged users.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RD Gateway Connection Authorization Policy (CAP) Changed
description: An RD Gateway Connection Authorization Policy was changed, which governs which users/groups and under what conditions (e.g. device redirection, idle timeout) may authenticate through the Gateway at all.

data_sources.name: RD Gateway management event log
data_sources.description: Policy configuration change events.

detection_logic: Filters CAP configuration change events.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype=<rdgw_mgmt_sourcetype> action="cap_changed"
| table _time, user, policy_name
tuning_guidance: Low volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Review the specific policy change for broadened access.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RD Gateway Resource Authorization Policy (RAP) Changed
description: An RD Gateway Resource Authorization Policy was changed, which governs which internal hosts/groups an authenticated Gateway user may connect to — a broadened RAP directly expands lateral-movement reach through the Gateway.

data_sources.name: RD Gateway management event log
data_sources.description: Policy configuration change events.

detection_logic: Filters RAP configuration change events.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype=<rdgw_mgmt_sourcetype> action="rap_changed"
| table _time, user, policy_name
tuning_guidance: Low volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Review the specific resource scope change for over-broadening.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RD Gateway Service Stopped
description: The RD Gateway service stopped, which will block all Gateway-mediated RDP access until it restarts.

data_sources.name: System Event Log
data_sources.description: Service Control Manager stop events for the RD Gateway service.

detection_logic: Filters System log Service Control Manager events for the RD Gateway service.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:System" EventCode=7036 service_name="TSGateway" state="stopped"
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: Correlate with maintenance windows.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Restart if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RD Gateway Certificate Replaced
description: The TLS certificate presented by RD Gateway was replaced, which — while legitimate during scheduled rotation — could indicate an attacker-controlled certificate enabling interception if the issuer is unrecognized.

data_sources.name: RD Gateway management event log
data_sources.description: Certificate replacement events.

detection_logic: Filters certificate binding change events for the Gateway.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype=<rdgw_mgmt_sourcetype> action="cert_bound"
| table _time, user, cert_issuer, cert_thumbprint
tuning_guidance: Confirm against the approved internal or public CA issuer; expected during scheduled rotation.
investigation_steps: Verify the issuer against the approved CA.
response_guidance: Revert if the issuer is unrecognized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RD Web Access Brute Force / First-Seen Source
description: Repeated authentication failures or a first-seen source against the RD Web Access portal, the web-front-end analogue of RDP-GW-001/RDP-GW-003.

data_sources.name: IIS log / RD Web application log
data_sources.path: Authentication events on the RD Web Access application
data_sources.description: Web-tier authentication telemetry.

detection_logic: Counts RD Web Access authentication failures per source in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype=<iis_sourcetype> cs_uri_stem="*/RDWeb/*" sc_status=401
| bin _time span=10m
| stats count by _time src
| where count>=10
tuning_guidance: Tune against known scanning noise if the portal is Internet-facing.
investigation_steps: Block the source if unrecognized.
response_guidance: Block the source.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RD Connection Broker Session Host Membership Changed
description: A session host was added to or removed from an RD Connection Broker collection, changing which servers are eligible to receive load-balanced or reconnected sessions — an attacker-added rogue session host would be positioned to receive real user sessions.

data_sources.name: RD Connection Broker management event log
data_sources.description: Session host membership changes.

detection_logic: Filters Connection Broker collection membership change events.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype=<rdcb_mgmt_sourcetype> action="session_host_membership_changed"
| table _time, user, session_host, collection
tuning_guidance: Confirm against change tickets for planned RDS farm scaling.
investigation_steps: Verify the added/removed session host is a legitimate, managed server.
response_guidance: Remove an unauthorized session host immediately; treat it as a likely rogue collection point.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Privileged Tooling Launched via RemoteApp
description: A RemoteApp launch invoked a general-purpose administrative tool (e.g. cmd.exe, PowerShell) rather than the specific published application, which — since RemoteApp is meant to expose only a narrow, published application surface — is atypical and can indicate an attacker abusing a RemoteApp entry point to obtain broader shell access.

data_sources.name: RemoteApp launch log
data_sources.description: RemoteApp launch events with the invoked application name.

detection_logic: Filters RemoteApp launch events where the application field references a general-purpose shell/administrative tool.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-RemoteConnectionManager/Operational" EventCode=1149
| where application IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","mmc.exe")
| table _time, user, src, application
tuning_guidance: Confirm this is not a deliberately-published administrative RemoteApp (rare but possible in specific admin-tooling deployments).
investigation_steps: Verify against the published RemoteApp catalog for this collection.
response_guidance: Remove the publication if unintended; investigate the session's subsequent activity.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1219: Remote Access Tools

author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Session Started
description: An RDP session was logged on via the Terminal Services LocalSessionManager channel. Complements Security 4624 with session-specific detail (session ID) needed for later reconnect/hijack correlation.

data_sources.name: TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager
data_sources.description: Session logon events with session ID.

detection_logic: Filters the LocalSessionManager channel for session logon events.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager/Operational" EventCode=21
| table _time, host, user, session_id
tuning_guidance: Not independently alertable; feed into the reconnect/hijack detections below.
investigation_steps: Correlate with Security 4624 for the corresponding source IP.
response_guidance: No independent response.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Session Disconnected
description: An RDP session was disconnected (not logged off), leaving it available for reconnection — the state that RDP-TS-006's hijack detection depends on.

data_sources.name: TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager
data_sources.description: Session disconnect events.

detection_logic: Filters the LocalSessionManager channel for session disconnect events.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager/Operational" EventCode=24
| table _time, host, user, session_id
tuning_guidance: Not independently alertable; building block for reconnect-abuse detections.
investigation_steps: No standalone investigation.
response_guidance: No independent response.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Session Reconnected from Different Source IP
description: A disconnected RDP session was reconnected from a source IP different from the one that originally established it, which is atypical for a legitimate user reconnecting from the same device/location and is the core signal for potential session hijacking.

data_sources.name: TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager + Security
data_sources.path: Session reconnect events joined against the session's original source IP
data_sources.description: Requires correlating session ID across the disconnect/reconnect lifecycle.

detection_logic: Compares the source IP at session reconnect (Security 4624 with Logon Type 10 for an existing session ID) against the source IP recorded at the session's original logon.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager/Operational" EventCode=25
| lookup session_origin_src.csv session_id OUTPUT original_src
| where src!=original_src
| table _time, host, user, session_id, original_src, src
tuning_guidance: Correlate with known NAT/VPN egress changes that can shift the observed source IP for a legitimate same-user reconnect.
investigation_steps: Treat as a likely session hijacking attempt.
Confirm with the original user whether they initiated this reconnect.
response_guidance: Terminate the session immediately if unconfirmed and force a credential reset for the account.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1563: Remote Service Session Hijacking

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Privileged Account Session Reconnect Anomaly
description: A privileged account's RDP session was reconnected from a different source, combining the severity of RDP-TS-003 with the elevated impact of a privileged session.

data_sources.name: TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager
data_sources.path: Session reconnect events for privileged accounts specifically
data_sources.description: Same as RDP-TS-003, scoped to privileged accounts.

detection_logic: Same as RDP-TS-003, filtered to accounts in the privileged-account lookup.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager/Operational" EventCode=25
| lookup session_origin_src.csv session_id OUTPUT original_src
| lookup privileged_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_privileged
| where src!=original_src AND is_privileged=1
| table _time, host, user, session_id, original_src, src
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate for a privileged account.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Confirm with the account owner immediately.
response_guidance: Terminate the session and disable the account pending investigation.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1563: Remote Service Session Hijacking

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Long-Dormant Disconnected Session Revived
description: A session that had been disconnected for an extended period was reconnected, which — beyond an ordinary short disconnect/reconnect cycle — is more consistent with an attacker discovering and reusing an abandoned session than a user resuming normal work.

data_sources.name: TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager
data_sources.path: Session reconnect events with elapsed disconnect duration
data_sources.description: Requires tracking the disconnect timestamp per session ID.

detection_logic: Computes elapsed time between a session's disconnect and reconnect events and flags long durations.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager/Operational" (EventCode=24 OR EventCode=25)
| eval stage=if(EventCode=24,"disconnect","reconnect")
| transaction session_id maxspan=30d startswith=eval(stage="disconnect") endswith=eval(stage="reconnect")
| eval disconnect_duration=duration
| where disconnect_duration>86400
| table _time, host, user, session_id, disconnect_duration
tuning_guidance: Tune the dormancy threshold to your environment's typical work patterns (e.g. return from vacation/leave).
investigation_steps: Confirm with the user whether they intentionally left the session disconnected this long.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1563: Remote Service Session Hijacking

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Session Reconnect Without Corresponding Fresh Authentication
description: A session state change to a reconnected/active state occurs without a corresponding Security 4624 authentication event, which is atypical for a normal RDP reconnect and can indicate session takeover via a lower-level mechanism (e.g. tscon.exe session redirection) that bypasses the usual authentication path.

data_sources.name: TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager + Security
data_sources.path: Session state-change events with no corresponding logon event
data_sources.description: Cross-channel gap detection.

detection_logic: Flags session reconnect/active events in the LocalSessionManager channel with no corresponding Security 4624 event within a tight window.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager/Operational" EventCode=25
| join type=left session_id [
    search index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
    | eval has_auth=1
  ]
| where isnull(has_auth)
| table _time, host, session_id
tuning_guidance: Verify the join window/logic against your specific TA's field extraction before relying on this in production.
investigation_steps: Treat as a strong session-hijacking indicator.
Correlate with tscon.exe execution (RDP-PROC-###).
response_guidance: Terminate the session and investigate the host for tscon-based hijacking.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1563: Remote Service Session Hijacking

author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Session Shadowing / Remote Control Started
description: An administrator initiated a Remote Desktop Shadow session (remote-control/view of another user's active session), a legitimate support feature that can also be abused to observe a victim's credentials, sensitive data, or session activity without their awareness if consent prompts are disabled.

data_sources.name: TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager
data_sources.description: Shadow session start events.

detection_logic: Filters the LocalSessionManager channel for shadow-session-start events.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager/Operational" EventCode=59
| table _time, host, shadowing_user, target_user
tuning_guidance: Baseline the small set of expected helpdesk/support accounts that use shadowing.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification with the shadowing account and the target user's awareness.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed; verify Group Policy requires user consent for shadowing.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1563: Remote Service Session Hijacking

author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Shadowing Without User Consent
description: A shadow session was established with the no-consent-required policy configuration, which given the target user has no visibility that they are being observed, is a covert surveillance capability that should never be enabled outside a very narrowly-scoped, well-governed support exception.

data_sources.name: TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager
data_sources.description: Shadow session events flagged as not requiring consent.

detection_logic: Filters shadow-session events where the consent flag indicates no consent was required/prompted.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager/Operational" EventCode=59 consent_required=0
| table _time, host, shadowing_user, target_user
tuning_guidance: Alert on all occurrences unless the organization has an explicit, narrowly-scoped, documented exception for no-consent shadowing (e.g. specific kiosk/lab management).
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Verify Group Policy for shadowing consent requirements.
response_guidance: Terminate the shadow session and correct the consent policy.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1563: Remote Service Session Hijacking

author: Threat Detection Library

title: tscon.exe Execution
description: tscon.exe was executed, the built-in Windows utility for connecting to an existing Terminal Services session — a well-documented technique (often run as SYSTEM via a scheduled task) to take over another user's disconnected session, including a Domain Admin's, without needing their password.

data_sources.name: Security 4688 / Sysmon Event ID 1
data_sources.description: Process-creation telemetry.

detection_logic: Filters process-creation events for tscon.exe.
spl:
index=<windows_index> (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4688 OR sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=1) process_name="tscon.exe"
| table _time, host, user, command_line
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume; RDS administrators rarely need this directly.
investigation_steps: Identify the target session ID in the command line and the account it belongs to.
Treat as a confirmed session-hijack attempt if the executing account differs from the target session's owner.
response_guidance: Terminate the target session and investigate the executing account/host as compromised.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1563: Remote Service Session Hijacking

author: Threat Detection Library

title: tscon.exe Targeting Another User's Session
description: tscon.exe was invoked with a /dest parameter targeting a session ID belonging to a different, currently-logged-on user, the confirmed hijack pattern rather than just tscon.exe's presence — this is the specific technique that lets an attacker running as SYSTEM take over a Domain Admin's disconnected session without any password.

data_sources.name: Security 4688 / Sysmon Event ID 1
data_sources.path: tscon.exe invocations with a /dest parameter, cross-referenced against session ownership
data_sources.description: Requires session-ownership lookup.

detection_logic: Extracts the target session ID from tscon.exe's command line and compares its owner against the executing account.
spl:
index=<windows_index> (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4688 OR sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=1) process_name="tscon.exe"
| rex field=command_line "/dest:(?<target_session>\S+)"
| lookup session_owners.csv target_session OUTPUT target_session_owner
| where isnotnull(target_session_owner) AND target_session_owner!=user
| table _time, host, user, command_line, target_session_owner
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; there is no legitimate reason for a different account to redirect into another user's session outside a rare, explicitly-approved support scenario.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed active session-hijack incident.
Immediately disable both the executing and target accounts pending investigation.
response_guidance: Full incident response: isolate the host, disable both accounts, and audit everything done under the hijacked identity.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1563: Remote Service Session Hijacking

author: Threat Detection Library

title: mstsc.exe Launched with /admin Flag
description: mstsc.exe was launched with the /admin flag, connecting to the destination's Session 0 console session (or, on modern Windows, Restricted Admin-adjacent behavior) rather than a standard user session — worth tracking as a less-common connection mode typically reserved for specific administrative scenarios.

data_sources.name: Security 4688 / Sysmon Event ID 1
data_sources.path: mstsc.exe process creation with /admin in the command line
data_sources.description: Process command-line telemetry.

detection_logic: Filters mstsc.exe process-creation events with the /admin flag.
spl:
index=<windows_index> (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4688 OR sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=1) process_name="mstsc.exe" command_line="*\/admin*"
| table _time, host, user, command_line
tuning_guidance: Baseline expected administrative use; escalate for unusual accounts/hosts.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: mstsc.exe Launched by Service Account
description: mstsc.exe was executed under a service/automation account context, which is atypical since RDP client usage is inherently interactive and service accounts should not normally have an interactive desktop session at all.

data_sources.name: Security 4688 / Sysmon Event ID 1
data_sources.path: mstsc.exe process creation joined against a service-account lookup
data_sources.description: Process-creation telemetry.

detection_logic: Filters mstsc.exe process-creation events where the executing account is in the service-account lookup.
spl:
index=<windows_index> (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4688 OR sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=1) process_name="mstsc.exe"
| lookup service_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_service_account
| where is_service_account=1
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained service-account lookup; low expected false-positive rate.
investigation_steps: Treat as a likely credential-compromise indicator.
response_guidance: Rotate the service account credential and investigate the host.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: New .rdp File Created in Temp/Downloads
description: A .rdp connection file was created in a Downloads or Temp directory, consistent with a phishing lure or malicious document delivering a pre-configured RDP connection (potentially with malicious redirection settings) rather than a user manually creating a saved connection profile.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 11
data_sources.path: File-creation events for .rdp files in Downloads/Temp
data_sources.description: File-creation telemetry.

detection_logic: Filters file-creation events for .rdp extension files in Downloads/Temp/email-attachment-staging directories.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=11
| where match(target_filename, "(?i)\.rdp$") AND match(target_filename, "(?i)(\\Downloads\\|\\Temp\\|\\INetCache\\)")
| table _time, host, user, target_filename
tuning_guidance: Expect some benign false positives; correlate with the delivery mechanism (email attachment, browser download) and whether the file is subsequently launched (RDP-TS-014).
investigation_steps: Inspect the
rdp file's contents for the target server and any redirection settings before it is launched
response_guidance: Quarantine the file and warn the user if unconfirmed.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Downloaded .rdp File Launched Shortly After Creation
description: A .rdp file created in Downloads/Temp (RDP-TS-013) was launched (via mstsc.exe) shortly after creation, confirming the user opened a lure/attachment-delivered RDP connection — worth prioritizing since malicious .rdp files can enable resource redirection attacks (giving the destination server access to the local clipboard, drives, and devices).

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 11 + Security 4688
data_sources.path: File-creation event for a .rdp file joined with a subsequent mstsc.exe launch of that file
data_sources.description: Sequence correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences a .rdp file-creation event with a subsequent mstsc.exe launch referencing that file within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<windows_index> sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=11 target_filename="*.rdp")
OR (index=<windows_index> (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4688 OR sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=1) process_name="mstsc.exe")
| eval stage=case(EventCode=11,"1_create", true(),"2_launch")
| transaction host user maxspan=10m startswith=eval(stage="1_create") endswith=eval(stage="2_launch")
| table _time, host, user, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Correlate with the delivery mechanism (email/browser) to confirm phishing origin.
investigation_steps: Identify the destination server the
rdp file connected to and whether it is attacker-controlled
response_guidance: Treat as a potential resource-redirection attack; investigate what local resources (clipboard, drives) may have been exposed to the remote server.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Drive Redirection Enabled on Sensitive Server
description: Local drive redirection was permitted for an RDP session to a host tagged as sensitive (Tier-0/Tier-1), giving the connecting client's local drives visibility inside the remote session — a documented data-transfer path for moving tooling in or data out that bypasses normal file-transfer monitoring.

data_sources.name: Terminal Services policy/session event log
data_sources.path: Session redirection policy state joined against a sensitive-host asset lookup
data_sources.description: Redirection state at session establishment.

detection_logic: Filters session-establishment events where drive redirection is enabled, joined against a sensitive-host lookup.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-RemoteDesktopServices-SessionServices/Operational" drive_redirection_enabled=1
| lookup asset_criticality.csv host OUTPUT tier
| where tier IN ("tier0","tier1")
| table _time, host, user, drive_redirection_enabled
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a documented policy allowing drive redirection to sensitive hosts (rare; most Tier-0/1 hardening baselines disable this entirely).
investigation_steps: Verify Group Policy for the destination host disables drive redirection per hardening baseline.
response_guidance: Disable drive redirection on this host via GPO if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Clipboard Redirection Used on Sensitive Server
description: Clipboard redirection was actively used during a session to a Tier-0/Tier-1 host, which — while a routine convenience feature — can also be a data-exfiltration path for copying credential material, keys, or sensitive text out of a hardened environment.

data_sources.name: Terminal Services session event log
data_sources.path: Clipboard redirection usage events, where the specific telemetry source exposes them
data_sources.description: This library does not claim clipboard content is visible — only that redirection was used, where the environment's specific telemetry stack exposes that signal.

detection_logic: Filters clipboard-redirection-use events (where exposed by the specific telemetry stack), joined against a sensitive-host lookup.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype=<rds_channel_audit_sourcetype> channel="cliprdr" action="data_transferred"
| lookup asset_criticality.csv host OUTPUT tier
| where tier IN ("tier0","tier1")
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: Clearly state telemetry limitations: standard Windows Event Log channels do not natively expose clipboard-redirection usage events by default in most configurations — this detection depends on a specific auditing/EDR capability being present, and this library does not claim it is universally available.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for clipboard use on this host.
response_guidance: Disable clipboard redirection on hardened Tier-0/1 hosts via GPO if this capability is not required.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Network Level Authentication Disabled
description: Network Level Authentication was disabled on a host, removing the pre-session-establishment authentication requirement and exposing the RDP service's full session-negotiation surface to unauthenticated connections — a foundational hardening control whose removal should be treated with the highest scrutiny.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: NLA requirement configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters registry/policy-change events for the NLA requirement setting moving to disabled.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=13 registry_path="*UserAuthentication*" new_value=0
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: Requires registry-change auditing (Sysmon Event ID 13 is the more reliable source in most environments; the Security-log equivalent is shown here for completeness) on the specific Terminal Server security-layer registry value — validate the exact path per Windows version before deployment.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Re-enable NLA immediately.
response_guidance: Re-enable NLA and audit any RDP access that occurred while it was disabled.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Security Layer Weakened
description: The RDP security layer setting was changed from a stronger mode (SSL/TLS or Negotiate) to the legacy RDP Security Layer, which uses weaker, non-standards-based encryption and lacks server authentication.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Security layer configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters security-layer configuration-change events for a weakening transition.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=13 registry_path="*SecurityLayer*"
| where new_value<old_value
| table _time, host, user, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification (rare: legacy client compatibility).
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Encryption Level Reduced
description: The RDP minimum encryption level was reduced (e.g. from High/FIPS to Low/Client Compatible), weakening the cryptographic protection of the session.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Encryption-level configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters encryption-level configuration-change events for a weakening transition.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=13 registry_path="*MinEncryptionLevel*"
| where new_value<old_value
| table _time, host, user, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Restricted Admin Mode Enabled
description: Restricted Admin Mode was enabled for RDP, which allows administrators to authenticate without sending reusable plaintext-equivalent credentials to the target — a legitimate hardening feature, but one worth tracking since its use also means the connecting user's credentials are not fully validated against the target and can enable pass-the-hash-style lateral movement if the connecting host is compromised.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Restricted Admin Mode configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters Restricted Admin Mode configuration-change events.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=13 registry_path="*DisableRestrictedAdmin*" new_value=0
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: This is a legitimate, often-recommended hardening feature — do not treat every occurrence as malicious. Escalate only when combined with other suspicious indicators (e.g. use from an unexpected source).
investigation_steps: Confirm this matches documented policy for Restricted Admin usage
response_guidance: No independent response; context-dependent.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Restricted Admin Mode Used for Privileged Remote Authentication
description: A privileged account authenticated using Restricted Admin Mode from a source host outside the expected set of hardened administrative jump hosts, which is worth extra scrutiny since Restricted Admin from a compromised or lower-trust source can enable an attacker with local admin on that source to pivot using cached credential material.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Restricted Admin logon events (identifiable via specific logon package/authentication package fields) joined against an expected-jump-host lookup.

detection_logic: Filters Restricted-Admin-mode logon events for privileged accounts and joins against an expected-jump-host lookup.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10 authentication_package="Negotiate" restricted_admin_mode=1
| lookup privileged_accounts.csv user OUTPUT is_privileged
| lookup approved_jump_hosts.csv src OUTPUT is_approved
| where is_privileged=1 AND isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, user, src, dest
tuning_guidance: Requires an identifiable Restricted Admin flag in the parsed logon event and a maintained jump-host allowlist.
investigation_steps: Confirm the source host's trust level and patch/hardening state.
response_guidance: Investigate if the source is not an approved hardened jump host.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: CredSSP Encryption Oracle Remediation Weakened
description: The CredSSP Encryption Oracle Remediation policy was set to a less-secure enforcement level (e.g. 'Vulnerable' instead of 'Force Updated Clients'), reintroducing exposure to the well-documented CVE-2018-0886 CredSSP RCE class of vulnerability. Validate the exact policy name/values against current Microsoft documentation before deployment, since these have changed across patch releases.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: CredSSP Encryption Oracle Remediation configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters CredSSP remediation-level configuration-change events for a weakening transition.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=13 registry_path="*CredSSP\\Parameters*AllowEncryptionOracle*"
| where new_value<old_value
| table _time, host, user, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume; alert on all occurrences, and treat any host still at the vulnerable setting as a patching-compliance finding independent of this change-based detection.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification (rare: legacy client compatibility during a migration window).
response_guidance: Revert to Force Updated Clients if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Enabled on Endpoint or Server
description: Remote Desktop was enabled on a host (registry fDenyTSConnections set to 0), expanding the RDP attack surface by one more listening host.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: RDP enablement configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters RDP-enablement configuration-change events.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=13 registry_path="*fDenyTSConnections*" new_value=0
| table _time, host, user
tuning_guidance: Expected during planned server provisioning; require a change ticket for enablement on general workstations, where RDP is typically disabled by default policy.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification, especially on workstation-class hosts.
response_guidance: Disable if unauthorized.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1021.001: Remote Desktop Protocol

author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Listening Port Changed from Default
description: The RDP listener port was changed from the default 3389, which can be legitimate obfuscation-as-a-defense but is more commonly seen as an attacker technique to evade port-based firewall/detection rules on an already-compromised host running a backdoor RDP listener.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: RDP port configuration-change events.

detection_logic: Filters RDP port configuration-change events.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=13 registry_path="*PortNumber*" service_context="TermService"
| table _time, host, user, old_port, new_port
tuning_guidance: Confirm against a documented, organization-wide non-standard-port policy if one exists; otherwise treat as suspicious by default.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Correlate with RDP-NET-009 for network-level confirmation of the new listener.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Remote Desktop Firewall Rule Broadened to Any Source
description: The built-in Windows Firewall 'Remote Desktop' rule's remote address scope was changed to Any, removing whatever source-IP restriction previously limited RDP exposure on this specific host.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Windows Firewall rule-modification events (4947/4950) for the Remote Desktop rule group.

detection_logic: Filters Windows Firewall rule-modification events for the Remote Desktop rule group where the remote address scope is set to Any.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode IN (4947,4950) rule_name="*Remote Desktop*"
| where new_remote_addresses="*" OR new_remote_addresses="Any"
| table _time, host, user, rule_name, new_remote_addresses
tuning_guidance: Very low expected volume outside a deliberate exposure decision; alert on all occurrences.
investigation_steps: Treat as a critical exposure finding.
Combine with RDP-NET-001 to confirm actual inbound traffic.
response_guidance: Revert immediately unless this is the organization's approved, monitored RD Gateway host.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Group Policy Weakening (NLA/Encryption/Redirection/Timeout)
description: A GPO governing Remote Desktop security settings (NLA requirement, encryption level, session timeouts, redirection permissions, Remote Credential Guard, or password-saving) was modified to a weaker configuration, which — unlike a single-host registry change — propagates to every computer object the GPO applies to.

data_sources.name: AD Group Policy Object change log
data_sources.path: GPO modification events for Terminal Services/Remote Desktop policy settings
data_sources.description: GPO setting-change events.

detection_logic: Filters GPO modification events for Terminal Services security-relevant settings moving to a weaker value.
spl:
index=<ad_index> sourcetype=<ad_audit_sourcetype> event_type="gpo_setting_changed"
| where match(setting, "(?i)(TerminalServices|RemoteDesktop)") AND weakened=1
| table _time, user, gpo_name, setting, old_value, new_value
tuning_guidance: Requires GPO change auditing (Group Policy Management Console versioning or AD audit logs); very high value given the fleet-wide blast radius of a single GPO change.
investigation_steps: Identify every computer object the GPO applies to and assess exposure.
Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Revert immediately if unauthorized; the fleet-wide impact makes this a priority even without an active exploitation signal.

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1484: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification

author: Threat Detection Library

title: User Added to Local Remote Desktop Users Group
description: An account was added to the local Remote Desktop Users group on a host, granting it RDP logon rights independent of any domain-level group membership.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Local group membership change events (4732) for the Remote Desktop Users group.

detection_logic: Filters local group membership change events for the Remote Desktop Users group.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4732 group_name="Remote Desktop Users"
| table _time, host, user, target_user
tuning_guidance: Confirm against onboarding change tickets; low volume in most environments.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification with the requesting manager.
response_guidance: Remove if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Same Account Added to Remote Desktop Users Across Many Hosts
description: The same account was added to the local Remote Desktop Users group on an unusually large number of distinct hosts within a short window, expanding a single account's RDP reach fleet-wide.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log (fleet-aggregated)
data_sources.description: Distinct-host count for Remote Desktop Users additions per target account.

detection_logic: Counts distinct hosts where the same account was added to Remote Desktop Users in a rolling window.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4732 group_name="Remote Desktop Users"
| bin _time span=1h
| stats dc(host) as hosts_affected by _time target_user
| where hosts_affected>=5
tuning_guidance: Tune out known fleet-provisioning automation.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for such broad access.
response_guidance: Investigate and revert if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: User Added to Local Administrators Followed by RDP Login
description: The specification's core privilege-to-access chain: an account was added to the local Administrators group and, within a short window, that account established an RDP session — worth the highest scrutiny when the adding source is unusual.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Local Administrators group addition event followed by an RDP logon event for the same account.

detection_logic: Sequences a local Administrators group addition event with a subsequent RDP logon event for the same account within a bounded window.
spl:
index=<windows_index> (EventCode=4732 group_name="Administrators") OR (EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10)
| eval stage=case(EventCode=4732,"1_admin_add", true(),"2_rdp_login")
| transaction host target_user maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_admin_add") endswith=eval(stage="2_rdp_login")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=2
| table _time, host, target_user, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Treat as Critical when the source performing the addition is unusual; very low expected false-positive rate overall.
investigation_steps: Treat as a live incident.
Confirm business justification for both the privilege grant and the immediate login.
response_guidance: Disable the account, revert the privilege grant, and investigate the granting account for broader compromise.
author: Threat Detection Library

threshold.baseline_condition: local admin addition -> RDP login, same account

title: Explicit Credential Use Followed by Outbound RDP Connection
description: An explicit-credential logon event (Security 4648, used when a process authenticates with credentials different from the current session, such as runas or an application supplying alternate credentials) is followed by an outbound RDP connection from the same host, which can indicate an attacker using harvested or alternate credentials to pivot via RDP. Not every explicit-credential event is RDP-related — this detection correlates specifically with a subsequent outbound RDP session as the confirming signal.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log + network telemetry
data_sources.path: Explicit-credential logon event joined with a subsequent outbound RDP connection from the same host
data_sources.description: Sequence correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences a Security 4648 explicit-credential-use event with a subsequent outbound TCP/3389 connection from the same host within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<windows_index> sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4648)
OR (index=<network_index> dest_port=3389)
| eval stage=case(EventCode=4648,"1_explicit_cred", true(),"2_outbound_rdp")
| transaction host maxspan=10m startswith=eval(stage="1_explicit_cred") endswith=eval(stage="2_outbound_rdp")
| table _time, host, eventcount
tuning_guidance: High false-positive rate given how many legitimate processes use explicit credentials for non-RDP purposes; use as a supporting/investigative signal rather than a standalone high-confidence alert.
investigation_steps: Identify the specific credential and destination used
response_guidance: Investigate the credential source if the resulting RDP destination is unexpected.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Suspicious Process Executed in Active RDP Session
description: A process from the specification's watch-list (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe, wscript.exe, cscript.exe, mshta.exe, rundll32.exe, regsvr32.exe, certutil.exe, bitsadmin.exe, curl.exe, wget, net.exe, net1.exe, nltest.exe) was launched within the process tree of an active RDP session, worth baseline scrutiny given how often these tools appear in post-exploitation activity.

data_sources.name: Security 4688 / Sysmon Event ID 1
data_sources.path: Process creation events correlated to a session ID with an active RDP logon
data_sources.description: Requires linking process creation to the originating RDP session ID.

detection_logic: Joins process-creation events against active RDP session IDs and filters for a watch-list of commonly-abused tools.
spl:
index=<windows_index> (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4688 OR sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=1)
| lookup active_rdp_sessions.csv session_id OUTPUT is_rdp_session
| where is_rdp_session=1
| where process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","nltest.exe")
| table _time, host, user, session_id, process_name, command_line
tuning_guidance: Requires session-ID correlation between logon and process-creation events; tune against normal administrative tooling.
investigation_steps: Review the full command line and parent process.
response_guidance: Escalate severity if this precedes discovery/credential-access/persistence activity (RDP-PROC-002 through 004).

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1059: Command and Scripting Interpreter

author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Login Followed by Discovery Commands
description: An RDP login is followed within 10-30 minutes by discovery commands (whoami, ipconfig, netstat, nltest, quser, net group), the classic post-access reconnaissance pattern used to establish situational awareness on a newly-accessed host.

data_sources.name: Security 4688 / Sysmon Event ID 1
data_sources.path: RDP logon event joined with subsequent discovery-tool process creation on the same host/session
data_sources.description: Sequence correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences an RDP logon event with subsequent discovery-tool process creation on the same host within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10)
OR (index=<windows_index> (sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4688 OR sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=1) process_name IN ("whoami.exe","ipconfig.exe","netstat.exe","nltest.exe","quser.exe","qwinsta.exe","net.exe","net1.exe"))
| eval stage=case(EventCode=4624,"1_login", true(),"2_discovery")
| transaction host user maxspan=30m startswith=eval(stage="1_login") endswith=eval(stage="2_discovery")
| table _time, host, user, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Very common for legitimate administrators too; escalate primarily based on the account/source's overall risk context (first-seen, privileged, off-hours) rather than this sequence alone.
investigation_steps: Review the full sequence of discovery commands run.
response_guidance: Escalate if followed by credential access or persistence (RDP-PROC-003/004).

references.title: MITRE ATT&CK T1082: System Information Discovery
MITRE ATT&CK T1016: System Network Configuration Discovery
MITRE ATT&CK T1049: System Network Connections Discovery
MITRE ATT&CK T1033: System Owner/User Discovery

author: Threat Detection Library

title: RDP Login Followed by Credential Access Activity
description: An RDP login is followed by LSASS memory access, credential-dumping tool execution, browser credential-store access, or SAM/SECURITY/SYSTEM registry hive access — one of the highest-priority post-RDP-compromise sequences, since a successful credential dump can propagate the compromise well beyond the single host.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 10 (ProcessAccess) / EDR credential-access detections
data_sources.path: LSASS access events or known credential-dumping tool execution following an RDP logon
data_sources.description: Requires Sysmon process-access auditing or equivalent EDR telemetry.

detection_logic: Sequences an RDP logon event with subsequent LSASS process-access or known credential-dumping tool execution on the same host within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10)
OR (index=<windows_index> sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=10 target_process="lsass.exe")
| eval stage=case(EventCode=4624,"1_login", true(),"2_lsass_access")
| transaction host maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_login") endswith=eval(stage="2_lsass_access")
| table _time, host, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Tune out known, approved EDR/AV processes that legitimately access LSASS for scanning purposes via a process allowlist.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed credential-theft incident.
Assume every credential on the host is compromised.
response_guidance: Isolate the host, force a domain-wide credential reset for any account that had a session on this host, and engage full incident response.

title: RDP Login Followed by Persistence Mechanism Creation
description: An RDP login is followed by creation of a scheduled task, a new service, a Run-key registry modification, or a new local/domain account — the standard post-access persistence-establishment pattern.

data_sources.name: Security/System Event Log + Sysmon
data_sources.path: RDP logon event joined with subsequent persistence-mechanism-creation events on the same host
data_sources.description: Sequence correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences an RDP logon event with a subsequent scheduled-task/service/Run-key/account-creation event on the same host within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10)
OR (index=<windows_index> (EventCode=4698 OR EventCode=4720 OR EventCode=7045) OR (sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=13 registry_path="*\\Run\\*"))
| eval stage=case(EventCode=4624,"1_login", true(),"2_persistence")
| transaction host maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_login") endswith=eval(stage="2_persistence")
| table _time, host, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Correlate with the account's normal administrative duties; a routine RDP support session followed by legitimate service work will also trigger this.
investigation_steps: Review the specific persistence mechanism created and its business justification.
response_guidance: Remove the persistence mechanism if unauthorized and investigate the RDP session's full activity.

title: RDP Login Followed by Security Control Impairment
description: An RDP login is followed by Microsoft Defender being disabled, Windows Firewall being changed, event logs being cleared, or an EDR agent being stopped — the specification's named post-RDP defense-evasion pattern and a strong precursor to more damaging follow-on activity.

data_sources.name: Security/System Event Log + EDR
data_sources.path: RDP logon event joined with subsequent security-control-impairment events on the same host
data_sources.description: Sequence correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences an RDP logon event with a subsequent security-control-impairment event (Defender disabled, firewall changed, log cleared, EDR stopped) on the same host within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10)
OR (index=<windows_index> (EventCode=1116 OR EventCode=5025 OR EventCode=1102) OR (sourcetype=<edr_sourcetype> action="agent_stopped"))
| eval stage=case(EventCode=4624,"1_login", true(),"2_impairment")
| transaction host maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_login") endswith=eval(stage="2_impairment")
| table _time, host, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; treat as a critical incident.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed active incident.
Assume subsequent activity on this host is unmonitored/untrustworthy.
response_guidance: Isolate the host at the network level immediately and restore security controls out-of-band.

title: RDP Login Followed by Lateral Movement from the Same Host
description: An RDP login to Host A is followed by outbound RDP, SMB, or WinRM connections originating from Host A to other hosts, confirming Host A is being used as a pivot point — one of the highest-value lateral-movement pivot detections in this catalogue.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log + network telemetry
data_sources.path: Inbound RDP logon joined with subsequent outbound RDP/SMB/WinRM connections from the same host
data_sources.description: Sequence correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences an inbound RDP logon to Host A with subsequent outbound RDP/SMB/WinRM connections originating from Host A within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10 dest=host)
OR (index=<network_index> src=host dest_port IN (3389,445,5985,5986))
| eval stage=case(EventCode=4624,"1_inbound_rdp", true(),"2_outbound_pivot")
| transaction host maxspan=1h startswith=eval(stage="1_inbound_rdp") endswith=eval(stage="2_outbound_pivot")
| table _time, host, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate for a pivot pattern outside known jump-host behavior; tune out approved jump hosts specifically (they are expected to exhibit this pattern routinely).
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed lateral-movement pivot.
Identify every downstream host reached from this pivot.
response_guidance: Isolate Host A and every downstream host reached; treat the entire chain as compromised.

title: Rare RDP Destination Count for User
description: A user's daily distinct-RDP-destination count is well above their own historical baseline, a general-purpose behavioral backstop complementing the fixed-threshold fan-out detection (RDP-001).

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Per-user distinct-destination count compared against a trailing baseline.

detection_logic: Compares each user's daily distinct-destination count against their own trailing 30-day average.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| bin _time span=1d
| stats dc(dest) as daily_targets by _time user
| lookup user_rdp_baseline.csv user OUTPUT avg_daily_targets
| where daily_targets > (avg_daily_targets*3)
| table _time, user, daily_targets, avg_daily_targets
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained per-user baseline; expect noise for users with genuinely variable administrative workloads.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the elevated activity.
response_guidance: Investigate if unconfirmed.

title: Unusual RDP Session Duration
description: An RDP session's duration is well outside the user's or destination's typical range (either unusually long or a burst of many unusually short sessions), a general behavioral signal for both security and operational hygiene.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Session duration computed from logon/logoff pairs, compared against a baseline.

detection_logic: Computes session duration from paired logon/logoff events and compares against a per-user/destination baseline.
spl:
index=<windows_index> (EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10) OR (EventCode=4634)
| transaction user dest maxspan=24h startswith=eval(EventCode=4624) endswith=eval(EventCode=4634)
| eval duration_minutes=round(duration/60,1)
| lookup session_duration_baseline.csv user, dest OUTPUT avg_duration_minutes
| where duration_minutes > (avg_duration_minutes*5) OR duration_minutes < 1
| table _time, user, dest, duration_minutes, avg_duration_minutes
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained baseline; useful for both security anomaly detection and RDS capacity/hygiene planning.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the anomalous duration.
response_guidance: Low urgency alone.

title: First RDP Connection to a Given Destination
description: A destination host received its first-ever recorded RDP logon, worth tracking for newly-provisioned hosts (expected) versus long-standing hosts suddenly receiving RDP traffic for the first time (worth a closer look).

data_sources.name: Security Event Log
data_sources.description: Successful logon events joined against a per-destination first-seen-RDP baseline.

detection_logic: Joins successful RDP logon events against a rolling first-seen-destination baseline.
spl:
index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| lookup dest_first_rdp_baseline.csv dest OUTPUT first_seen
| where isnull(first_seen)
| lookup asset_provisioning_date.csv dest OUTPUT provisioned_date
| where provisioned_date=="" OR now()-strptime(provisioned_date,"%Y-%m-%d")>2592000
| table _time, user, src, dest
tuning_guidance: Correlate against the asset-provisioning date to distinguish a newly-built host (expected) from an established host receiving RDP for the first time (worth investigation).
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification if the host is not newly provisioned.
response_guidance: Low urgency for new hosts; investigate for established hosts.
