title: RDP Login Followed by Security-Control Impairment and Mass File Modification
description: The specification's named ransomware-precursor chain: an RDP login is followed by security-service impairment (RDP-PROC-005) and then a burst of file-modification activity consistent with encryption, the complete pattern for a human-operated ransomware deployment via RDP.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log + Sysmon/EDR file-activity telemetry
data_sources.path: RDP login, security-control impairment, and mass file-modification events chained for the same host
data_sources.description: Full destructive-chain correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences an RDP login, a security-control-impairment event, and a high-volume file-modification/rename burst on the same host within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10)
OR (index=<windows_index> (EventCode=1116 OR EventCode=5025))
OR (index=<windows_index> sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=11)
| eval stage=case(EventCode=4624,"1_login", EventCode=1116 OR EventCode=5025,"2_impair", EventCode=11,"3_file_activity", true(), null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=2h startswith=eval(stage="1_login")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=3
| eval file_events=mvcount(mvfilter(match(stage,"3_file_activity")))
| where file_events>=100
| table _time, host, eventcount, file_events
tuning_guidance: Treat any fully-corroborated instance as a confirmed severe incident; the individual component detections (RDP-PROC-005) should already have alerted.
investigation_steps: This is a confirmed ransomware incident — engage full incident response immediately.
Isolate the host and every host it had lateral-movement connectivity to.
response_guidance: Full incident response: network isolation, backup verification, and broad credential rotation for every account with a session on this host recently.

title: RDP Session Followed by Archive Creation and Large Outbound Transfer
description: An RDP session is followed by archive-utility execution (creating a compressed bundle) and then a large outbound network transfer, the specification's named exfiltration pattern.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log + Sysmon + network telemetry
data_sources.path: RDP login, archive-tool execution, and large outbound transfer chained for the same host
data_sources.description: Sequence correlation across endpoint and network telemetry.

detection_logic: Sequences an RDP login, an archive-utility process execution (7z, WinRAR, tar, Compress-Archive), and a large outbound network transfer from the same host within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10)
OR (index=<windows_index> sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=1 process_name IN ("7z.exe","winrar.exe","tar.exe","powershell.exe"))
OR (index=<network_index> bytes_out>104857600)
| eval stage=case(EventCode=4624,"1_login", process_name!="","2_archive", bytes_out>0,"3_transfer", true(), null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction host maxspan=2h startswith=eval(stage="1_login")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=3
| table _time, host, eventcount
tuning_guidance: This library does not claim Windows RDP logs alone provide complete file-transfer visibility — this detection explicitly requires network-level transfer-volume telemetry; tune the byte threshold to your environment.
investigation_steps: Identify the archive contents and the transfer destination.
response_guidance: Block the destination if unrecognized and investigate the data collected.

title: Alternative/First-Seen RDP Client Executable
description: An RDP client connection was initiated by an executable other than the standard mstsc.exe and not on the organization's allowlist of approved alternative clients (e.g. a specific third-party RDP client), which may be entirely benign but is worth classifying rather than assuming malicious by default per the specification's own caution against over-flagging every non-mstsc client.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 3 (network connection) + process telemetry
data_sources.path: Outbound TCP/3389 connections attributed to a non-mstsc, non-allowlisted process
data_sources.description: Requires process-to-network-connection attribution.

detection_logic: Filters outbound TCP/3389 network connections attributed to a process other than mstsc.exe, joined against an approved-alternative-client allowlist.
spl:
index=<windows_index> sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=3 dest_port=3389
| where process_name!="mstsc.exe"
| lookup approved_rdp_clients.csv process_name OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| table _time, host, user, process_name
tuning_guidance: Maintain an allowlist of approved third-party RDP clients (e.g. Remote Desktop Connection Manager, specific MDM-deployed clients) to avoid flagging routine legitimate tooling; classify findings as approved/unknown/suspicious rather than treating every hit as malicious.
investigation_steps: Identify the process and determine whether it should be added to the approved-client allowlist or investigated further.
response_guidance: Investigate unknown/unclassified clients; no action needed for newly-approved ones once added to the allowlist.

title: VPN Compromise Leading to RDP Fan-Out
description: The specification's core VPN-to-RDP chain: repeated VPN authentication failures are followed by a VPN success, then an RDP success, then internal RDP fan-out — the complete path from an external credential attack through to internal lateral movement, elevating RDP-006 into a full end-to-end incident view.

data_sources.name: VPN log + Security Event Log
data_sources.path: VPN failure/success sequence joined with subsequent RDP success and fan-out for the same user
data_sources.description: Full multi-stage correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences VPN authentication failures, a VPN success, an RDP success, and RDP fan-out for the same user within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<vpn_index> (action="failure" OR action="success"))
OR (index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10)
| eval stage=case(index=<vpn_index> AND action="failure","1_vpn_fail", index=<vpn_index> AND action="success","2_vpn_success", true(),"3_rdp")
| transaction user maxspan=2h startswith=eval(stage="1_vpn_fail")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=3
| stats dc(dest) as rdp_targets by user
| where rdp_targets>=3
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; treat as a confirmed multi-stage incident.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed active incident.
Disable both VPN and domain accounts immediately.
response_guidance: Full incident response spanning VPN and every internal host reached.

title: AD Privilege Escalation Leading to RDP
description: The specification's core AD-to-RDP chain: a user is added to an administrative group and, within a short window, RDPs into a server or domain controller — elevating RDP-CFG-013's single-host detection into a full identity-plus-access incident view spanning any destination.

data_sources.name: AD Group Membership Changes + Security Event Log
data_sources.path: Privilege-grant events joined with subsequent RDP logon events for the same account
data_sources.description: Full identity-to-access correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences an AD administrative-group addition event with a subsequent RDP logon event for the same account within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<ad_index> sourcetype=<ad_audit_sourcetype> EventCode IN (4728,4732) group_name="*Admins*")
OR (index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10)
| eval stage=case(group_name!="","1_privilege", true(),"2_rdp")
| transaction user maxspan=2h startswith=eval(stage="1_privilege") endswith=eval(stage="2_rdp")
| table _time, user, dest, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; treat as a live incident.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed privilege-escalation-to-access incident.
Revert the privilege grant and disable the account.
response_guidance: Full incident response.

title: RDP Compromise to Credential Theft
description: The specification's named RDP-compromise-to-credential-theft chain: a successful RDP login (especially one following repeated failures, RDP-AUTH-005) is directly followed by LSASS access — restated as a top-level cross-platform correlation combining the highest-confidence authentication and credential-access signals in the catalogue.

data_sources.name: Security Event Log + Sysmon
data_sources.path: RDP login after repeated failures joined with subsequent LSASS access
data_sources.description: Full authentication-to-credential-theft correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences a success-after-failures RDP login with subsequent LSASS process access on the same host within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<windows_index> (EventCode=4624 OR EventCode=4625) Logon_Type=10)
OR (index=<windows_index> sourcetype=<sysmon_sourcetype> EventCode=10 target_process="lsass.exe")
| eval outcome=case(EventCode=4624,"success", EventCode=4625,"failure", true(),"lsass_access")
| sort 0 user host _time
| streamstats time_window=15m count(eval(outcome="failure")) as failures by user host
| where (outcome="success" AND failures>=5) OR outcome="lsass_access"
| transaction host maxspan=1h startswith=eval(outcome="success" AND failures>=5) endswith=eval(outcome="lsass_access")
| table _time, host, user, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; treat as a confirmed incident.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed credential-theft incident.
Rotate every credential exposed on this host.
response_guidance: Full incident response.

title: Firewall Exposure Leading to Brute Force and Compromise
description: The specification's named exposure-to-compromise chain: a firewall rule change exposes RDP to the Internet, followed by inbound brute-force attempts, followed by a successful login — the complete path from a configuration mistake to an actual breach, tying together RDP-NET-002, RDP-NET-001, and RDP-AUTH-005 into a single incident view.

data_sources.name: Firewall change log + network telemetry + Security Event Log
data_sources.path: Firewall exposure event, inbound brute-force traffic, and a successful login chained together
data_sources.description: Full multi-stage correlation.

detection_logic: Sequences a firewall rule change exposing RDP, subsequent inbound brute-force traffic, and a subsequent successful login within a bounded window.
spl:
(index=<firewall_index> action="rule_changed" dest_port=3389)
OR (index=<windows_index> EventCode=4625 Logon_Type=10)
OR (index=<windows_index> EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10)
| eval stage=case(action="rule_changed","1_exposure", EventCode=4625,"2_bruteforce", EventCode=4624,"3_success", true(), null())
| where isnotnull(stage)
| transaction dest maxspan=24h startswith=eval(stage="1_exposure")
| where mvcount(mvdedup(stage))>=3
| table _time, dest, eventcount
tuning_guidance: Very low expected false-positive rate; treat as a confirmed breach originating from a configuration error.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed active breach.
Close the exposure immediately and investigate the compromised account/host.
response_guidance: Full incident response: close the firewall exposure, disable the compromised account, and isolate the host.
